threshold_status: PROTOTYPE. Limits are team-chosen and NOT clinically validated; the NASA HRP pages the team extracted give hazard context, not per-vital limits. Context for each indicator is named in 'source'.

resource_math.notes: Simulated Closed-Loop ECLSS Estimates (decision support, not life-support design). Context: NASA HRP Hostile/Closed Environments video, as transcribed by the team: 'Close the loop - Recycling all possible resources, including an astronaut's carbon dioxide and urine, into tomorrow's Air and Water.' extra_kcal = (MET - rest_met) * mass_kg * hours. CO2 is derived from standard respiratory physiology: respiratory quotient 0.85 (dimensionless, NOT g/kcal) at 4.86 kcal per L O2 gives 0.175 L CO2 per kcal, about 0.34 g/kcal at STP. Water 1.15 mL/kcal and all MET values are team simulation assumptions.

radiation.note: Context: NASA HRP Space Radiation: mission effective doses range from about 50 to 2,000 mSv (1 mSv is roughly 10 chest X-rays); ISS crews get about 10x Earth's dose; deep space adds Solar Particle Events (solar flares, 11-year cycle) and Galactic Cosmic Rays. Daily expected rates below are scenario presets derived from that range, not measurements.

compliance.streak_goal: morning_vitals_logged AND resistive >= low_fraction*target AND ration >= low_pct

immune_risk.note: Elevated radiation AND (mild temp rise OR mild sleep drop). RED only via temp's own absolute limit. Context: NASA HRP Hostile/Closed Environments: stress hormones, radiation and poor sleep alter immunity.

indicators.label: Resting heart rate
indicators.source: team prototype. Context: NASA HRP Gravity (cardiovascular adaptation, arrhythmia risk) and Radiation (circulatory disease)

indicators.label: Systolic BP
indicators.source: team prototype; low side ADDED. Context: NASA HRP Gravity (fluid shift, low BP and fainting on landing; countered by lower-body compression and fluid loading)

indicators.label: Diastolic BP
indicators.source: ADDED (team listed SBP/DBP but gave no DBP limits); team prototype

indicators.label: Fasting glucose
indicators.source: team prototype; 126-140 gap closed (yellow), low yellow 70 ADDED. Context: NASA HRP Isolation (limited food variety, nutritional deficiency)

indicators.label: Core temperature
indicators.source: team prototype. Context: NASA HRP Hostile/Closed Environments (altered immunity, infections, microbes passing between crewmates)

indicators.label: Sleep duration
indicators.source: team prototype; floor raised 0.5 -> 1.0 h (see test_engine test 4). Context: NASA HRP Isolation (circadian misalignment; a Martian sol is 24 h 38 min; NASA tracks lighting, movement and sleep with wrist actigraphy)

indicators.label: Mood (1-10)
indicators.source: ADDED absolute limits (team prototype); RED means 'contact crew psychologist / flight surgeon', not an emergency. Context: NASA HRP Isolation (mood, morale, cognition decline; crew journaling as a countermeasure)

indicators.label: PVT reaction time
indicators.source: team prototype; browser and mouse latency add a few tens of ms, so the anchor Z matters more than the absolute limits. Context: NASA HRP Gravity (fine motor skills, spatial orientation, hand-eye coordination) and Radiation (CNS effects on cognition and motor function)

indicators.label: Cabin CO2
indicators.source: team prototype limits; no official CO2 limit was extracted from the NASA HRP pages. Context: NASA HRP Hostile/Closed Environments habitability factor 'Air'

indicators.label: Radiation dose rate
indicators.source: judged against the environment's expected rate (ratio rule); an elevated ratio is surfaced as a possible Solar Particle Event (solar flare) alert. Context: NASA HRP Space Radiation

indicators.label: Resistive exercise
indicators.input_0g: Crew log (ARED on station; any resistive device elsewhere)
indicators.source: team rule: <30 min for 3+ days in microgravity -> YELLOW. Context: NASA HRP Gravity (spine and hips lose about 1-1.5% mineral density per month in microgravity; ISS crews exercise about 2 h/day in total)

indicators.label: Ration intake
indicators.source: team rule: <80% -> nutrition flag (2-day confirm and RED tier ADDED). Context: NASA HRP Radiation (nausea, anorexia) and Isolation (food variety)

indicators.label: Immune risk (composite)
indicators.source: team rule: elevated radiation + mild temp rise or sleep drop. Context: NASA HRP Hostile/Closed Environments (stress hormones + radiation + poor sleep alter immunity)

SPACE_STATION.label: Space station (LEO)
SPACE_STATION.source: Scenario preset. NASA HRP Distance: ISS is about 250 miles (~402 km) up. NASA HRP Space Radiation: ISS crews get about 10x Earth's dose; 50-100 mSv over a ~6-month stay is 0.27-0.55 mSv/day, preset 0.4.

DEEP_SPACECRAFT.label: Deep-space transit to Mars
DEEP_SPACECRAFT.source: Scenario preset. NASA HRP Distance: Mars averages about 140 million miles (~225 million km, the slider default); NASA quotes delays up to ~20 min one way, the app computes 3.0-22.3 min from distance/c. NASA HRP Space Radiation: multi-year missions approach 500-2,000 mSv, roughly 1.0-1.8 mSv/day; preset is the 1.4 midpoint. Slider min/max are Earth-Mars orbital geometry.

PLANETARY_BASE_MOON.label: Lunar base
PLANETARY_BASE_MOON.source: Scenario preset. NASA HRP Distance: Moon is 238,855 miles (~384,400 km). Radiation preset sits in the same deep-space range (no magnetic-field protection). Gravity 0.16 g.

PLANETARY_BASE_MARS.label: Mars base
PLANETARY_BASE_MARS.source: Scenario preset. NASA HRP Gravity: Mars surface is 3/8 g (0.375 g). Radiation preset is the low end of the 1.0-1.8 mSv/day range, a simulation assumption (NASA's pages give no separate surface rate).

SURFACE_ROVER_MOON.label: Lunar rover
SURFACE_ROVER_MOON.source: Scenario preset, same radiation and distance as the lunar base; small cabin gives a higher CO2 default (simulation assumption).

SURFACE_ROVER_MARS.label: Mars rover
SURFACE_ROVER_MARS.source: Scenario preset, same as the Mars base; small cabin gives a higher CO2 default (simulation assumption).
